messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Mixture with Matt trick
messages.subject_clean: [stan-users] Mixture with Matt trick
messages.body_plain:
OK, I think I see what you're trying to do --- use
a normal mixture as a hierarchical prior.

To apply the Matt trick to a mixture prior, you have to
do the summation over the usage of the variable.

Suppose the total model is this, with lambda being the
mixture probability and mu and sigma the vectors of mixture
component parameters:

  p(y,z,mu,sigma,lambda)
  =
    p(mu, sigma, lambda)        // priors
    * p(y | mu, sigma, lambda)  // mixture for y
    * p(z | y)                  // conditioning z on y

For example, with the suggested two-component normal mixture,
the density for y is:

  p(y|mu,sigma,lambda)
    =  lambda * normal(y|mu[1],sigma[1]) + (1 - lambda) * normal(y|mu[2],sigma[2])

And suppose for concreteness that

  p(z | y) = foo(z | y)

Then you can do the mixture with a non-centered (Matt tricked)
parameterization this way in Stan on the log scale:

  parameters {
    real y_raw;
  }
  model {
    y_raw ~ normal(0,1);
    increment_log_prob(
      log_sum_exp(log(lambda) + foo_log(z, mu[1] + sigma[1] * y_raw),
                  log1m(lambda) + foo_log(z, mu[2] + sigma[2] * y_raw) ) );
    ... prior log p(lambda,mu,sigma) ...
  }

This should work very well because y_raw should mix just fine compared
to trying to sample for y.  I'm pretty sure I have this right, but it'd
be nice if someone else could check my logic here.

You don't get samples for y out, but you do get mu and sigma (as well
as lambda if you let that be a parameter instead of fixing at 0.5).  You
could generate them in generated quantities as you did elsewhere.

- Bob

P.S.  I also added a feature request for mixture functions on the log scale
to make writing mixture models a bit easier:

  https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/970

That'd be:

  log_mixture(real lambda, real lp1, real lp2)
    = log_sum_exp(log(lambda) + lp1, log1m(lambda) + lp2)

where lambda must be in (0,1).  And another more general version

  log_mixture(vector theta, vector lp)
    = log_sum_exp(log(theta) + lp)

where theta is a K-simplex and lp a K-vector.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] how to constrain the sum of variables to stay positive
messages.subject_clean: [stan-users] how to constrain the sum of variables to stay positive
messages.body_plain:
The constraint is essentially an ordering constraint.  The model is an graded response IRT model, in which category thresholds are decomposed into a item-specific and person-specific component.  The item thresholds can be declared as an ordered vector.  The person components are not necessarily ordered, but the sum of the person and item components is an ordered vector.  So each person component depends on the distance between item thresholds and the adjacent person component.  For example, if the minimum distance between two item thresholds is z, and the person components of those two thresholds are x and y, respectively, then x < z + y.

I've tried declaring a (person x item x category) array of ordered vectors, but it becomes prohibitively large.  Declaring the array as a local variable would work, but it looks like local variables need to be basic variable types.  It's tricky, but I think the constraint is coming from a reasonable assumption: that individuals may differ in the extent to which they are willing to endorse "good" versus "very good," (or some similar categories), but that those tendencies do not change the rank ordering of categories.

messages.subject: RStan Not Honoring Specified Inits?
messages.subject_clean: RStan Not Honoring Specified Inits?
messages.body_plain:
I have a model that has a kind of multi-modal posterior due to a reflection invariance.

Is pseudo-code, I have two generalized IRT-like models:
ResponseA[j,k]~Dist(Link( a[k] + b[k]*LatentDimA[j]))

ResponseB[j,k]~Dist(Link( c[k] + d[k]*LatentDimB[j]))

Followed by a Cobbs-Douglas parameterized Poisson regression
Outcome[j]~Poisson(exp(  g1 + g2*log(Age) + g3*log(LatentDimA) + g4*log(LatentDimB) ))

There there is a reflection invariance between both the b[k]s and g3, and the d[k]s and g4, since the responses can 'load backward' on the latent dimension.

I don't want to impose any positive constraints on the model parameters to impose identification. Rather I want to start the chain at various inits, defining b,d,g3,and g4 in order to target the specific modes of the posterior, and check if the modes are just reflections.

However, when I try to define inits=0, or inits=INITS, which I specify myself, RStan does not seem to honor them. Instead, when i used get_inits() after I fit the model, I get a different set of inits.

So, my question is, Whats going on here? How do I get RStan to honor my defined inits?

Also, with this kind of model specification, is there a way of forcing the latent dimensions to never 'load backward'?

messages.body_plain:
Hi Cody,

Regarding the subject of your email:

Initial values specified as inits=0 are on the unconstrained scale. If you have any constrained parameters, e.g. "real<lower=0> sigma", then an initial value of 0 on the unconstrained scale does not equal 0 on the constrained scale. See the chapter on transforms in the Stan manual for details on transforms.

I'm not sure which scale inits=INITS is specifying the initial values.

Nonidentifiability is an issue. If you're model is running slow, you'll have to address that. If it's running fast enough, there won't be harm in post processing, except for the fact that you haven't reached stationary in any single chain, which would be made clear if individual chains are not exploring all modes.

Daniel
